title: common: Cleanup manpage formatting
body:
Also address most troff issues. Not all of them are easy, in particular those manpages with long urls and examples that include digests are difficult to render in traditional manpages.

Add troff renderering to the Manpage to surface those troff issues more easily

comments.body:
Thanks for the detailed review!

I have rebased this PR onto the latest `main` and addressed all review feedback:

1. **Motivation & Scope**:
   - To clarify the ambition: this PR does **not** intend to re-word documentation or introduce semantic changes. The goal is strictly technical cleanup of man page formatting and troff rendering issues encountered during package builds.
   - While `mandoc` (standard on macOS/BSD) parses man pages into an AST and gracefully soft-breaks lines for terminals, `groff` (used by Debian/Ubuntu packaging QA, `man-db`, and lintian) is a physical typesetting engine. When encountering non-standard bullets (`·`, `▪`), malformed nested lists, unicode curved apostrophes (`’`), or unbreakable table columns, `groff` emits "cannot break line" / table overflow warnings or clips text. This PR ensures clean rendering on both `mandoc` and `groff`.

2. **Resolved Items**:
   - **`containers.conf.5.md`**: Fixed missing space before backtick (`read \`containers.conf\``) and removed the colon in `interface_name` (`\`device\``) for consistency with surrounding option lists.
   - **`containerignore.5.md`**: Restored the explicit `filepath.Clean` reference with standard ASCII apostrophes (`Go's filepath.Clean`) so exact semantics are preserved without troff issues. Kept existing line wrapping as requested.
   - **`Containerfile.5.md`**: Indented the SELinux relabeling explanation paragraphs under the `* relabel=...` bullet points so they are properly nested in Markdown renderers.
   - **`Makefile`**: Left untouched so macOS builds remain unaffected.

Ready for another look when you have a moment!
